[[File:Greyling 0S.png|thumb|A [[greyling]], an aggressive creature found in the [[Meadows]].]] '''Creatures''' are non-player characters which are found throughout ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''. They can be split to four categories: * [[Creatures#Bosses|Bosses]] are powerful aggressive creatures that must be summoned. Killing them unlocks [[Forsaken power|Forsaken powers]], increases [[Global Keys|world difficulty]] and provides loot to progress in the game. * [[Creatures#Minibosses|Minibosses]] are unique, named, aggressive creatures that you can find in specific dungeons. Killing any given miniboss will reward with one of [[Hildir's Chests]]. * [[Creatures#Aggressive creatures|Aggressive creatures]] will attack players when alerted. They also drop loot when killed. * [[Creatures#Passive creatures|Passive creatures]] provide resources when killed (or harvested). They will never attack players. * [[Creatures#NPCs|NPCs]] are friendly creatures/characters that cannot be killed and may provide some service or help to the player. == Bosses == Bosses, also known as the '''Forsaken''', can be summoned by offering specific items (hinted by the [[Runestone#Altar Runestones|Runestones]]) at their specific spawn site. They have increased HP and special attacks compared to regular creatures. A boss site is automatically marked on the player's map by reading the runestone in the specific biomes. There are multiple spawn locations for every boss. One-star creatures have double the health and deal 150% damage, while two-stars have triple the health and deal double damage. '''Behavior''' *Creatures will give up chasing after unable to attack for 60 seconds or unable to detect the target for 30 seconds. *Some creatures have a max chase range. After chasing that far they will give up if unable to detect the target for 1 seconds. *After unable to attack for 15 seconds, creatures will focus structures for 15 seconds if they can't reach the target. *Creatures only attack walls and doors if they aren't able to reach the target player. *Some creatures are afraid of fire and will flee from it. *Some creatures try to avoid fire and will be passive near it. *Some creatures circulate around the target while waiting to attack. *Swimming creatures try to flee towards water if forced on ground. *Creatures passively regenerate 1.67% of their max health every minute (100% over 60 minutes). *Creatures gain +30% more effective health per each additional player within 100 meters. E.g. 3 players = +60% effective health. **This is updated whenever the creature takes damage. *Creatures gain +4% more damage per each additional player within 100 meters. '''Mushrooms''' can be found on the ground in the [[Meadows]], [[Black Forest]] and [[Swamp]]. Picked mushrooms will respawn after 240 minutes, or {{duration|14400}}, at the same place that they were picked. Unlike the case with raspberries and blueberries, which do not return if the plant itself is removed, mushrooms will return if the ground is cleared or even excavated.

Mushrooms are almost negligible as a food, but they are a vital component of some of the best recipes in the later game, as well as being food for tame Boars. Since they cannot be cultivated, and do not grow in large numbers at any one place, it is prudent to save some of them from early in the game for later use.

== Collection strategies ==
Collecting large quantities of mushrooms can be tedious since they cannot be farmed with a cultivator. However, there are strategies to make mushroom collection more manageable. One of the simplest and most effective methods is to mark mushroom locations on your map. This can be done from the start of the game, helping you plan efficient foraging routes.

Additionally, once you have enough resources to create multiple portals, you can set up "portal chains" for rapid mushroom collection. Start by placing a portal at your base with a short name ending in "1". Travel to an area with a large mushroom patch, link up the first portal, and set up a new portal with the same name ending in "2", and continue to another mushroom-rich area. Repeat this process as many times as needed. Finally, place a return portal at the last location and link it back to your base. This setup allows for quick and easy mushroom collection every 240 minutes.

To keep track of the harvest time, use a pickable ground item near your mushroom portal to act as a timer. Since all ground items respawn every 240 minutes (4 hours), picking up an item at your base after a mushroom harvest will signal when it is time to harvest again once the item reappears.

'''Poison''' is a negative [[status effect]] that applies a damage overtime effect on the affected entity. It is caused by [[Damage types#Poison|Poison damage]].

All resistances like [[Poison Resistance Mead]] are applied at the time of creating the effect and ignored on tick. Therefore any change to resistances after the effect start doesn't change it.

=== Stacking ===
Poison damage does not stack. The effect calculates how much damage remains to be dealt, and if a new poisonous attacks deals more poison damage than the remaining one, the effect is re-created. Otherwise, that incoming damage is ignored.

== Calculations ==
Duration from total damage is calculated (see below for more precise numbers) as <math>\lceil (1 + \sqrt{X*damage}) \rceil</math> where X is 5 against players and 1 against enemies. This means Poison lasts roughly twice as long for players and halves the tick damage. See further section for the technical details.

Tick damage is calculated with <math>{total \ damage \over duration}</math>.

=== Extra damage ===
Theoretically, the total damage from all ticks should be the same as initial value, but due to rounding the total damage is slightly higher.

* First we take non-integer value of <math>duration</math> as: <math>1 + \sqrt{X*damage}</math>
* then we take <math>damagePerHit = \frac{totalDamage}{\lfloor duration \rfloor}</math>
* then actual number of ticks is <math>\lfloor \frac{duration}{1.02} \rfloor + 1</math>.

Where does this come from? Due to floating number peculiarities<ref>https://0.30000000000000004.com/</ref> and the fact, that Valheim runs physics on fixed 50 FPS, every tick takes 1.02 seconds, but since first tick happens at the beginning of duration, when time = 0, we have an extra one.

Here's a table with calculations for various damage values: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSrjL9LtSGBgIAgr7Y_9Kej79ZQ9bh70ND9pNOAeCA5axUGA-AEp4FKdGhra-co-8RdeMpB5TLrlsV-/pubhtml Poison damage google spreadsheets].

[[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] (-25%) VS pierce, slash, and blunt damage, -100% [[block]] stamina cost, +5 stamina returned per block.

==[[Moder]] Power==
{{Quote|The dragon's wings urge you on. You shall always have tailwind while sailing, and you shall swiftly carry heavy burdens, even over the coldest mountains.}}
Always tailwind when sailing, +300.0 increased [[carry weight]], +10% increased movement speed, [[Resistance|Resistant]] (-50%) vs frost.

===Notes===
*This power changes the [[wind]] direction while sailing, but not wind intensity. A calm wind will not aid in travel as much as a fast wind.
*The wind direction is only changed while steering the ship. While not in control of a ship, the wind will remain at its regular angle.
*The wind change is local to each player carrying the buff and does not affect each other's wind direction.
*This power is best saved for when there is headwind since crosswind (perpendicular to travel direction) and tailwind are about equally good for sailing.
*This power will not affect the wind if you are too close to the [[World Edge|World's Edge]].

==[[Yagluth]] Power==
{{Quote|The fallen king lends you his might. A king must have the power to vanquish his foes, just as he must be able to support his people.}}
Resistant (-50%) vs lightning, +25 [[Farming (skill)]], and +10% increased damage.

==[[The Queen|The Queen's]] Power==
{{Quote|Her Majesty blesses you. In her shadow both stealth and magic may flourish, and no poison shall harm you.}}
+100% [[Eitr]] regeneration increase, -100% [[sneak]] stamina usage, and resistant (-50%) vs poison.

== [[Fader]] Power ==
{{Quote|The Emerald Flame never relents. You shall stand your ground, even when it is aflame, and you shall use all the advantages the battle may offer you.}}
+100% [[Adrenaline]] increase, 50% reduced [[stagger]] meter modifier, and resistant (-50%) vs fire.

==Notes==
* Bonemass Power damage resistance does ''not'' stack with [[Crystal Heart]].
* [[Kall Fimbulbringer]] does not provide a Forsaken Power upon hanging his trophy on the Sacrificial Stones, as doing so ends the game instead.

'''Wisp Fountains''' are [[Player base|base]] structures used for collecting [[Wisp]]s, which will be attracted to the fountain when it is dark; either when it is night, or raining, in any biome. Torches and other artificial light sources do not prevent it from summoning wisps.  

They require a [[Stonecutter]] to be built.

== Notes ==
Wisps begin to appear around 18:00. They also appear when it is raining.

A new wisp will join the fountain every 30 seconds, with initially up to three wisps present at a time. Eventually, up to nine wisps can be present near morning.

Hovering over the fountain whilst it is dark enough to attract wisps, it will say, "The wisps are coming." Once the fountain has three wisps, the text will change to "The wisps are dancing." This seems to indicate the fountain has the maximum number of wisps circling it, but it is possible to have more, seemingly due to a bug or quirk in the way the wisp spawning works.

If the player has more than one fountain nearby, the maximum number of wisps is shared among them. Spread the fountains out by more than 20 meters to allow each to reach its maximum.

If they are not caught before the day comes, wisps will fly away and disappear. During the day, while hovering over the fountain, it will say, "The wisps demand darkness."

== Tips ==
* Wisps can also appear during the day if rainy or stormy weather conditions are active. Some players have observed that weather effects triggered by certain boss encounters (such as Eikthyr’s storm) can temporarily allow wisps to spawn even outside normal nighttime conditions, as long as the player remains within the affected area.

* Keeping strong wind active through weather events can also be useful for nearby wind-powered structures, such as windmills, allowing both wisp farming and production benefits at the same time.

* Because wisps will despawn once daylight returns and darkness conditions are no longer met, staying close to the source of the weather effect is required to maintain their appearance.

* In addition to nighttime, some biomes such as the Swamp provide permanent low-light environments, provided the area remains loaded by nearby players.

'''Ballistae''' are [[:Category:Misc structures|misc structures]] that act as an automated defense. 

A Ballista can hold 40 missiles of the same type, which will be depleted one at a time as it fires. By default, a Ballista will shoot at any [[Creatures|creature]] in an arc (±45 degrees) within a 28 meters range in front of it, including [[Player Character|player characters]] and [[Taming|tamed]] animals. Care should be taken when loading the Ballista, as it will begin shooting after the first missile is loaded if the player is standing within the firing arc.

Damage is solely based upon the [[Missiles|missile]] loaded ([[Wooden Missile]], [[Black Metal Missile]], or [[Flametal Missile]]).

==Targeting==
Targeting can be overridden by using [[trophies]]. The Ballista will usually only target and shoot enemies corresponding to the trophy used, with the exception of Draugr and Charred enemies. 
* Using trophies from [[Draugr]] or [[Draugr Elite]] will set the Ballista to target 'Draugr', including melee and ranged variants, as well as the Draugr Elite. 
* Using trophies from the [[Charred Warrior]], [[Charred Marksman]], or the [[Charred Warlock]] will set the Ballista to target 'Charred', including all of these enemies as well as the [[Charred Twitcher]]. 
* Only one trophy can be active at once, and it is not consumed, allowing for a single trophy to be used on any number of Ballistae. 
* Default targeting can be applied by using the same trophy again, or by dismantling and rebuilding the Ballista.

== Notes ==
* Considering their hostility to friendlies, such as other players and tames, in default targeting mode, caution and placement location is highly advised. Building structures which can be opened and closed, such as [[Wood Structures|wooden doors or wooden gates]], in front of the Ballista to block their field of vision ensures safe passing when needed.
* Ballistae have a slow and inaccurate aim, but quick shooting speed. Building [[Trap|traps]] to immobilize fast-moving enemies in the Ballista's range increase their effectiveness greatly. For bigger and/or slower enemies, the Ballista might need higher elevation to be effective, especially against flying creatures.
* Due to its universal target range, Ballistae can be used to train blocking skills. However, Ballistae ''cannot be parried'', so using [[Shields|tower shields]] in combination with wooden missiles due to lower damage is recommended. They can also serve as protection against other players in multiplayer servers, while still being mindful of the Ballista targeting its owner.

'''Chain lightning''' is an on-hit effect triggered by weapons upgraded with [[Iolite]] or [[Thunderblood Essence]].

==Effect==
Chain lightning has a 25% chance to trigger on a normal attack and a 20% chance to trigger on a secondary attack.

It deals 75 [[lightning]] damage to the target, the amount is not affected by skills, and it cannot be blocked or dodged.

Once triggered, it has an 80% chance of bouncing off nearby enemies or players. If so, each nearby target within 8 meters has a 30% chance of being targeted, up to a maximum of 2–4 targets per bounce (the maximum is chosen at random then targets are processed starting from the nearest). The process repeats indefinitely, centered on each new target, but with the chance of rebound multiplied by 0.75 each time (i.e., 80% → 60% → 45% → 33.75%, etc.).

A single activation of chain lightning cannot affect the same target more than once.

==Notes==
* Chain lightning within the vicinity of neutral [[Ashlands Dvergr]] has the potential of damaging them, immediately turning them hostile.
